content: The comparison between intermittently scanned continuous glucose monitoring (isCGM) and real-time continuous glucose monitoring (rtCGM) in diabetes management highlights the distinct advantages each system offers, tailored to the specific needs of patients. Both isCGM and rtCGM are extensively utilized tools in diabetes care, and clinical studies have demonstrated their efficacy in reducing hemoglobin A1C (HbA1c) levels. Additionally, both systems contribute to an improvement in the time patients spend within their target blood glucose range (Time in Range, TIR). However, rtCGM has been shown to provide superior outcomes in the management of hypoglycemia. This is primarily due to its ability to deliver real-time alerts and continuous feedback, which enable patients to respond promptly to fluctuations in blood glucose levels. These features make rtCGM particularly effective in preventing and managing episodes of low blood glucose.
